messages:
maria: Quick check — thinking about a cleanup/refactor of the continuous-batching scheduler. TL;DR: want to tighten queueing interfaces so admission/eviction are explicit and make headroom metrics first-class. looking for tradeoffs before i draft an RFC.

jake: +1. do you mean collapsing the admission facade and making a separate headroom service?

maria: Not a separate network service, more like a clear module boundary with a small API: ReserveTokens(tenant, tokens) / ReleaseTokens(tenant, tokens) / SnapshotHeadroom(). Move all heuristic accounting out of the scheduler core.

sunil: I like the modularity. main tradeoff is latency — another call path increases hotpath cost if we query SnapshotHeadroom synchronously during enqueue. can we keep a local cache with TTL?

liz: we already have a local credit ledger in the current impl. problem is drift under preemption + lease reassign. if we add TTL cache, need an eventual-consistency model and a way to reconcile without incorrect admission (ie avoid accepting >gpu-capacity).

ben: proposal: strong source-of-truth in the allocator, but expose a fast read-only in-memory view on each node. writes go through allocator async; reads read the local view. add a conservative reservation guard to protect the GPU.

maria: that seems reasonable. i'm worried about corner cases where a burst of small requests from many tenants beats the TTL and we overcommit. maybe add a short, cheap admission check that keeps a per-node soft cap.

jake: agree. soft cap + leaky-bucket per node. also, make eviction signals explicit: Evict(tenant, reason) so the runtime can do graceful kvcache drop vs hard terminate. current code has ad-hoc evictions.

sunil: +1 on explicit evict. also we should expose an evict-priority enum (LOW, MEDIUM, CRITICAL) so downstream components can choose: drop prefix-cache, then trim beams, then abort.

liz: ops-wise, we need telemetry: per-tenant admitted_tokens, outstanding_tokens, evictions_by_reason, headroom_staleness_ms. these are needed for SLO guardrails. without them we won't be able to tune TTL safely.

ben: question about queue topology: continue with single shared queue + admission ledger, or move to many micro-lanes per-tenant-range? micro-lanes reduce tail by isolating noisy tenants but complicate packing.

maria: i want to keep a hybrid: default shared queue for packing efficiency + optional pinned micro-lane for tenants with strict latency SLA. routing policy can pin. that keeps common-case efficiency and gives isolation when needed.

jake: yep. packing heuristics will need to know lane type — maybe lane metadata: {isolation_level, max_slots, burst_priority}. small config snippet:```
queue_config:
  default: {isolation_level: shared, max_slots: 1024}
  vip: {isolation_level: pinned, max_slots: 32, burst_priority: high}
```

sunil: love the config. runtime note: pkgs that do batching need to query lane metadata cheaply — include it in the local snapshot.

maria: open question: admission signals should be token- or request-count-based? tokens are good since we already account per-token for cost predictions, but for latency-critical tiny requests tokens ~ length=1 may behave oddly.

liz: we can dual-account: primary tokens for cost + a small request credit for microburst protection. REQUEST_CREDIT that depletes slower (one per request).

ben: plan for RFC then: 1) define admission API (Reserve/Release/SnapshotHeadroom) 2) explicit eviction API + priority enum 3) local read-only headroom snapshot with TTL + reconciliation hooks 4) hybrid queue topology + lane metadata 5) telemetry + RFC-proof POC for 2 weeks.

maria: sounds good. i'll sketch RFC and include a small POC plan for the local snapshot reconciliation tests. will call out metrics and a canary plan.

deploy-bot: deploy starting: batcher-refactor-poc -> staging (id: brpoc-2026-03-21-11).

jake: can we get a minimal test harness that fuzzes eviction order and TTL skew? i can write a small harness to simulate leases moving between nodes.

maria: yes please. include tests for: race between Reserve and Evict, local snapshot stale read leading to conservative denial, and micro-lane packing efficiency.

sunil: i'll add diagonal load profiles (many tiny vs few long) to the harness. this should show cost/latency tradeoffs.

liz: i'll add dashboards for the metrics above in the RFC so eng-sre can review during the canary.

maria: awesome — i'll post the RFC draft tomorrow. thanks all. :party-blob:
